reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) describes selective dissolution of non-noble metals (Cu, Ru) and formation of noble-metal shells (Pt, Pd) in aqueous/corrosive environments for catalysis, not thermal premelting/melting of FeNiCrCoCu HEA nanoparticles. The evidence does not address surface diffusion as the governing mechanism for phase transition onset, nor does it demonstrate that an external passivation layer delays melting. Key premises about thermal behavior and the specific HEA system are unsupported.
premises: Non-noble elements in alloy nanoparticles selectively dissolve from the surface at elevated temperature
Selective dissolution leads to formation of a noble-metal-rich surface shell (core–shell structure)
The formed noble shell acts as a passivation layer protecting the core from further dissolution
Surface diffusion is the mechanism enabling selective dissolution and shell formation
An externally applied passivation layer can inhibit surface diffusion and dissolution
